title: EU/US data routing & subprocessor responsibility - ApexCare security review
summary: A focused security review on EU/US data routing paths, responsibilities across Redwood and its subprocessors, KMS key management options, and technical constraints for VPC/private deployments. ApexCare is evaluating Private Redwoods (VPC) vs Dedicated capacity with strong emphasis on auditability, SSO/RBAC, and contractual subprocessor clauses.
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC 2 and ISO27001 artifacts and the current subprocessor CSV; due 2026-05-18
Maya to draft a VPC peering / private deployment network checklist and proposed latency test plan; due 2026-05-21
Sophie to circulate ApexCare DPA redline and list of mandatory contractual clauses; due 2026-05-28
action_items: Jordan Patel: Send SOC 2 report, ISO attestation, and current subprocessor inventory spreadsheet; due: 2026-05-18
Maya Chen: Prepare VPC peering diagram, test plan for latency and cross-region failover, and sample audit log exports; due: 2026-05-21
Sophie Lake (ApexCare): Share initial DPA redline and any mandatory data residency contract language; due: 2026-05-28
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Lena (CISO - ApexCare), Rajiv (Head Infra), Sophie (Legal)

Summary (auto): quick run through of Redwood hosting options, region pinning guarantees, KMS split approaches and who is liable for subprocessors. ApexCare asked for concrete artifacts (SOC2/ISO) and a VPC peering checklist.

00:00:12 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Thursday afternoon, appreciate it. We wanted to focus this session on the EU/US routing questions and the subprocessor responsibilities you flagged in the questionnaire. And Maya is here to go through the technical pieces.

00:00:35 Lena: Thanks Jordan. I think the key for us is to know exactly where customer data may traverse or be processed. We're regulated in the EU for patient data and have to prove residency and no unauthorized cross-border processing. So we need clear answers on what Redwood controls vs what the cloud providers do.

00:01:02 Rajiv: Yeah, and also to understand egress risk and KMS handling. We prefer a model where our keys live in our KMS but we need to know if there's any required token or key material that leaves EU boundaries.

00:01:28 Maya: Totally. Quick high-level: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC) deployments. For strict residency needs you can opt for Private — that's a customer VPC with our inference nodes running either as dedicated instances or in a bring-your-own infra pattern. But there are nuances around subprocessor services like our metrics + observability, and some optional backends.

00:01:55 Sophie: When you say "subprocessor" are you including the cloud infra (IaaS) as part of that chain? We need the full chain spelled out for our legal team.

00:02:10 Jordan: Yes, exactly. We treat cloud providers, monitoring, and any managed DBs that hold logs as subprocessors. We'll share a CSV of current subprocessors — that's in the action items. Note that the list can change but we publish notices and provide options for certain customers to restrict to approved regions.

00:02:38 Rajiv: Is there a way to lock processing to EU regions only, like a hard region-pin? We had a brief in the questionnaire but it wasn't granular.

00:02:50 Maya: We support region affinity and region pinning at request. For Hosted API, we do region affinity by routing, but it's not a legal guarantee of no cross-border processing — there's a fallback/failover policy that could route to a proximate region if needed. For Dedicated and Private, we can provide stronger guarantees — Private gives you full control over residency since the compute is in your VPC or a customer-dedicated cluster in a chosen region. There's also the concept of a 'geo-fence' policy we can apply — but for the strictest cases you should go Private or Dedicated pinned clusters.

00:03:28 Lena: That matches what we were hoping for. A few follow-ups — how do you handle audit logs? We need immutable logs for access and, ideally, a way to pull logs into our SIEM without them transiting through non-EU services.

00:03:48 Maya: Good question. We can stream audit logs to a customer-owned logging endpoint (e.g., a logging bucket or SIEM endpoint in your VPC) for Private deployments. For Dedicated, we provide a secure export mechanism and can configure retention. For Hosted, logs are in Redwood audit systems which are treated as subprocessors; we can export on request but there may be cross-region egress depending on your configured region.

00:04:15 Jordan: To add, we can do per-token audit traces and include token-level metadata for who/what called the model. Those traces are available via the Console and can be pushed to your endpoint. We'll demo that in the follow-up if you want.

00:04:40 Rajiv: On KMS — we want customer-managed keys. Does Redwood support split KMS where customer holds master key and Redwood holds a per-instance key? We are concerned about any plaintext key material leaving the EU.

00:04:56 Maya: We have several KMS patterns. Option A is Redwood-managed keys (fastest onboarding). Option B is customer-managed KMS (we encrypt model caches and token logs under your keys via CMKs — we call it a KMS-binding approach). Option C is an advanced split-key where the master key remains in your HSM and we use an escrow/unwrap flow that never exports the master key. In the split/escrow model we can perform crypto ops in-region; we do not persist key material outside the HSM. That model requires a Private or Dedicated deployment and an HSM integration.

00:05:38 Sophie: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO artifacts that show the controls around key management and subprocessor oversight? We need to attach those to our security questionnaire.

00:05:50 Jordan: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate — redacted for sensitive details — and a mapping of relevant controls. I'll attach them to the deal in your portal.

00:06:05 Lena: Do you support SSO with SAML/SCIM and RBAC for the Console? We want to ensure access control for operations and audit trail of who invoked deployments.

00:06:18 Maya: Yes, SSO (SAML) is supported, and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is configurable at role-level with separate permissions for Console actions and API tokens. For Private deployments you can map to your identity provider and we avoid storing passwords on our side.

00:06:40 Rajiv: About subprocessors — is there an SLA or contract clause that lets us approve or reject a new subprocessor? Sometimes cloud providers add services and we need to be notified.

00:06:54 Jordan: We publish an updated subprocessor registry and will notify customers via the Console and email for material changes. For enterprise contracts we can include DPA language that requires notice and gives a period to object. That's typically part of our enterprise legal negotiations.

00:07:12 Sophie: We'll need that explicit objection window in the contract. Also, do you support a requirement that logs and snapshots remain in-region for a set retention period?

00:07:25 Maya: For Private yes, you can enforce in-region retention. For Dedicated we can configure retention targets and data residency constraints but there may be managed services involved that require specific handling.

00:07:40 Lena: One slightly technical thing — our app concatenates patient records and sends as prompt prefixes. We need to know if KV cache or prefix caching could cause cross-tenant leakage if cache replication happens across regions.

00:07:57 Maya: Good callout. Our serving runtime uses tenant-isolated KV caches; we do not replicate KV cache contents across tenant boundaries. Replication for redundancy is regional and can be disabled in Private. For Dedicated we isolate caching to the cluster. There's also configurable cache TTLs. We'll include a short note about cache isolation in the artifacts.

00:08:25 Jordan: There was a question in the form about whether Redwood uses any US-based subprocessors for telemetry. The short answer is some monitoring and analytics partners are US-based for Hosted deployments, but customers with residency needs can opt out or select Private/Dedicated to avoid those paths.

00:08:46 Rajiv: If we go Dedicated in EU region, do we still get some control plane interactions that call home to Redwood in the US?

00:08:56 Maya: The control plane for Dedicated is multi-regional by default. For enterprise customers we have an option to run a private control plane in your account or in a customer-dedicated VPC — that eliminates cross-region control plane calls. That is part of the Private offering or an enterprise Dedicated add-on.

00:09:18 Sophie: Could you outline the residual risk for hosted vs dedicated vs private in a short bulleted form? Legal likes a concise risk matrix.

00:09:31 Jordan: Sure, quick bullets: Hosted = fastest, but has subprocessors and potential cross-region fallbacks; residual risk: medium-high for strict residency. Dedicated = dedicated compute in chosen region, reduced subprocessor surface but control plane may be multi-regional unless configured; residual risk: medium. Private (VPC/on-prem) = highest control, can achieve in-region processing and customer-managed KMS; residual risk: low assuming HSM/KMS and logging are configured. We'll send a one-pager.

00:10:05 Lena: Perfect. Regarding evidence: we need audit log exports in a format that our SIEM can consume (syslog or S3 bucket). You said you can stream logs to customer-owned buckets?

00:10:20 Maya: Yes, for Private we can deliver logs to an S3 bucket in your account or to a SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. For Dedicated we typically use a secure export to your logging bucket. Hosted is export-on-demand and might traverse our logging pipeline.

00:10:40 Rajiv: What about data deletion and backup snapshots? Are those always encrypted under customer keys?

00:10:49 Maya: Snapshots and backups can be encrypted under customer-managed keys when using CMK mode. We also have retention policies you can set per-deployment. For hosted customers we encrypt at rest but with Redwood-managed keys unless you opt into CMK options.

00:11:10 Sophie: Any examples of customers who run in Private for EU data sovereignty? We want references just to sanity-check operations.

00:11:20 Jordan: We can provide references; there are a few healthcare and finance customers who have Private deployments in EU. I'll check our reference policy and include relevant, approved contacts.

00:11:35 Lena: Switching to the subprocessor chain — we need the legal team to see the flow: where logs go, where telemetry is processed, which subprocessors have access to PII. Can you provide a diagram?

00:11:50 Maya: Yes, we'll provide a subprocessor matrix and a flow diagram showing control plane, data plane, logging, and monitoring — including region info and whether access is role-restricted.

00:12:05 Rajiv: Latency test plan — we need numbers for 99th percentile token latency from EU to a EU-hosted cluster vs fallback to US. We may need to simulate peak loads.

00:12:18 Maya: We can run a short benchmark in a Dedicated EU cluster and provide p50/p95/p99 numbers and a test harness you can run in your environment. That will also validate egress paths.

00:12:35 Jordan: Quick practical question from our side — what is ApexCare's timeline for procurement and compliance sign-off?

00:12:44 Sophie: We're aiming to finish security assessment by end of June, procurement by mid-July, and a pilot in August. That assumes vendor artifacts are provided promptly.

00:13:00 Jordan: Great, that fits our timelines. We'll prioritize the SOC2/ISO docs and the subprocessor file.

00:13:10 Lena: A technical nit: can you confirm whether any model weights or token caches ever get stored outside of the region during nightly maintenance tasks or model updates? We worry about maintenance windows causing ephemeral cross-region writes.

00:13:28 Maya: Model weights updates are typically pushed to nodes in-region. In Hosted we may stage artifacts to a global storage for distribution, but that process can be configured for enterprise customers to stage within EU only. For Private/Dedicated, artifacts are staged in your region. We'll include standard operating procedures for maintenance windows.

00:13:52 Rajiv: If we use customer-managed KMS, is there an option for split-escrow with your team so we can run crypto ops without exporting our master key? You mentioned that earlier but we need specifics.

00:14:05 Maya: Yes — the split-escrow pattern uses an on-prem HSM or cloud HSM in your account. We perform an unwrap operation in-region; we never store the master key. The flow is: Redwood requests a short-lived unwrap token, uses that to perform encryption ops, and then the token expires. We'll provide a tech note and sequence diagram.

00:14:30 Sophie: Liability: if a subprocessor causes a breach, what indemnity or contract language do you offer? We need the DPA to reflect subcontractor liability.

00:14:44 Jordan: We have standard DPA language that maps subprocessors and includes indemnity clauses. For enterprise we can negotiate more prescriptive clauses. I'll flag this with legal and include an example.

00:14:58 Lena: Auditability: do you support log signing or append-only storage for audit logs so that we can prove immutability?

00:15:08 Maya: We can support an append-only log export pattern — e.g., logs written to an S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled and server-side encryption with your CMK. That provides immutability and can satisfy many audit requirements.

00:15:25 Rajiv: Network diagram question — if we peered our VPC to Redwood nodes, will traffic go over private peering or does it still traverse the public internet?

00:15:34 Maya: With VPC peering or private interconnect we'll keep traffic on private links. For Private deployments we support AWS VPC peering, Azure ExpressRoute, and GCP Private Service Connect. We'll provide the list of supported peering types and the steps.

00:15:55 Jordan: I'm going to pull us back to the immediate deliverables so we don't lose momentum. The first deliverable is a subprocessor CSV and SOC2/ISO artifacts, second is VPC peering checklist and latency test plan, third is the DPA redline. Anything else from ApexCare?

00:16:12 Lena: It would help if you include a small risk matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private that our legal and security folks can triage quickly. Also a clear statement on whether you can run a private control plane in our EU tenancy or an on-prem control plane.

00:16:28 Sophie: Also, please include the notification process for new subprocessors and a sample objection workflow to be put into the contract.

00:16:39 Jordan: Got it. We'll bundle those into a single packet. Maya will own the tech artifacts and I will own the compliance deck and legal artifacts.

00:16:50 Maya: Quick interruption — Rajiv, one more follow-up: do you require encryption in transit between nodes within the cluster (e.g., TLS everywhere) in addition to KMS at rest?

00:17:02 Rajiv: Yes, TLS everywhere is a must. We also like mTLS for service-to-service.

00:17:09 Maya: We provide TLS and can support mTLS for Private. We'll include config details.

00:17:20 Lena: Any performance impact with mTLS and in-region KMS? We want to know tradeoffs.

00:17:28 Maya: Slight CPU overhead and some additional RTT for KMS unwrapping, but negligible at typical inference latencies if you use short-lived session keys and cache unwrapped keys locally. We'll include benchmark notes in the test plan.

00:17:44 Jordan: A few other quick questions from procurement: pricing delta between Hosted and Dedicated in EU region, and any minimum commitment for Dedicated. Sophie, we might need to loop in procurement later.

00:17:58 Sophie: Yes please. Pricing needs to be clear in the proposal. We prefer committed capacity if it reduces cross-border risk.

00:18:10 Jordan: Understood. We'll include a pricing appendix in the follow-up.

00:18:18 Lena: Any known limitations with Private regarding model variants or quantization? We use some larger models and want consistent latency.

00:18:30 Maya: Private supports the same model catalog, but some quantized variants require specific GPU drivers. We'll surface any compatibility notes per-model.

00:18:45 Rajiv: One last operational thing — who will be our primary point of contact for an incident and what's the on-call process?

00:18:55 Jordan: For enterprise/Private customers, we provide a named CSM and a technical account owner plus 24/7 incident escalation. We'll include a contacts table.

00:19:10 Sophie: Good. I have one contractual ask — can you provide a clause ensuring that any forensic data collected during an incident response remains in-region and is accessible to us?

00:19:21 Jordan: We can include a clause that forensic artifacts will be stored in-region and access will be granted to the customer, subject to applicable laws. We'll confirm language with legal.

00:19:35 Maya: OK since we're ~20 minutes in — do you want us to run a short demo of how the audit log export looks? We can share screenshots after.

00:19:44 Lena: Screenshots and a sample export are fine.

00:19:49 Jordan: Great. We'll compile the packet and attach to the CRM. Any other blockers or concerns?

00:19:58 Rajiv: Nothing else from infra side.

00:20:02 Sophie: No, that's it. We'll review the artifacts and send back the redline.

00:20:08 Jordan: Awesome, we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.

(Recording note: conversation continued with a few clarifying tech Qs and then wrap - 35m left in meeting for deeper technical deep dive which they opted to postpone and schedule a dedicated SE session next week)

00:36:12 Jordan: Quick recap — we will provide: SOC2 & ISO artifacts, subprocessor inventory CSV, region control plane options, VPC peering checklist and latency test plan, sample audit log exports, DPA redline example, and reference customers.

00:36:40 Lena: That's perfect. Please mark the SOC2 docs as redacted where needed.

00:36:48 Jordan: Will do. Maya, anything else you want to add?

00:36:52 Maya: I'll also include a short tech note on the KMS split-escrow flow and the cache isolation guarantees. I'll send the test harness so Rajiv can run it from their environment.

00:37:08 Sophie: We'll expect the DPA redline by 2026-05-28.

00:37:15 Jordan: Noted. We'll aim to get the docs to you by 2026-05-18.

00:37:22 Rajiv: Thanks all, looking forward to the plan.

00:37:26 Jordan: Thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: auto-generated transcript has several mis-heard acronyms (e.g., Redwood sometimes transcribed as 'RedWood' or 'Red wood'), mild punctuation issues and occasional speaker misattribution.
